text.p: The anti-Taleban alliance dropped at least four bombs during an air raid on Kabul's airport early on Sunday morning, military officials said.
There were no reports of casualties or major damage in the raid. The bombs from a single plane missed their target, landing outside the airport area at 1.15 a.m. (2045 GMT).

"The air raid did not hit inside the airport perimeter. Two or three bombs landed close to the residential area north of here, but there are no reports of casualties," said Faizullah (one name), the head of military security at the airport.
The night sky over Kabul was lit up as Taleban gunners fired tracer rounds and rocket-propelled grenades at the departing aircraft, but there was no sign it had been hit.

The airport is used for both military and civilian traffic and has been frequently targeted in the past. Both the International Committee of the Red Cross and the United Nations use it for the transport of staff and supplies.
A Red Cross flight arrived at the airport on Sunday morning after the bombing.
